label: yes
controls_available: Select individual ants by clicking the map or select a group with a marquee; Shift modifies the selection.
Press G, S, D, M, or R for GATHER, SCOUT, DIG, MARCH, or RAISE. In full mode the command is armed and a visible map destination is clicked.
GATHER targets the visible seed pile; SCOUT targets the listening front; DIG targets the brood chamber; MARCH targets NORTH, SOUTH, or the rival queen.
Pan the map with the minimap, its arrow buttons, or the left/right keys.
CERTIFY FRONT submits the command ledger and is administrative rather than outcome-affecting.
autonomous_processes: The match advances in 100 ms simulation ticks without new input. A scout progresses toward the listening front and, after 40 ticks at L3, contact is revealed and that worker automatically returns to GATHER.
Exactly two DIG workers add two brood-progress units per tick; at 70 units the brood becomes ready and those diggers automatically return to GATHER.
Workers assigned to GATHER make repeated seed trips and add one seed every 18 ticks.
RAISE spends two seeds and queues a soldier that appears at the rally point after 14 ticks.
A raid outpost expands before spawn. After spawn, the rival formation advances toward the colony while its visible vertical position oscillates through the tunnel approach.
At raid impact, the current defense commitment is evaluated, soldiers can be lost, the wave is resolved, and an unblocked raid damages the home queen.
After every raid is cleared, soldiers marching to the rival queen travel for 45 ticks and then damage it; the match terminates at 720 ticks if no win has occurred.
The CSS live pulse also animates without input, but it is decorative and changes neither task state nor outcome.
grouped_control_modes: GATHER: selected workers to the seed pile
SCOUT: one worker to the listening front
DIG: exactly two selected workers to the brood chamber
RAISE: no selected units; queue one soldier from ready brood
MARCH/intercept: selected soldiers to NORTH or SOUTH for an uncommitted raid inside its response band
MARCH/assault: selected surviving soldiers to the rival queen after all raids are cleared

clause_i.reason: Let D be all MARCH tunnel-commitment opportunities for the L3 raid. For identical prior actions and task times, the generator varies the seeded first lane and the 0-35-tick motion phase. At the delayed delivery time the maximizing target can therefore be NORTH in one history and SOUTH in another, while an action-clock-only q receives no current visual evidence and cannot select the correct target for every H_t in C_Delta(D).

clause_ii.reason: Six chronological frames over the configured 800 ms window show the formation's changing x/y position and, importantly, its vertical direction or reversal. That visible trajectory identifies the oscillation phase and predicts the NORTH/SOUTH target at t+800 ms, so a bounded-window policy g can select the appropriate soldiers and delayed tunnel from I_t and W_t^800. The full map exposes the formation, tunnel lanes, and intercept marker used for this decision.

clause_iii.reason: Use Delta=800 ms (8 simulation ticks) at a wave-1 history with at least four available soldiers, immediately before a visible vertical turning point and with the turn within the delay; take tau=300 ms. The formation autonomously reverses direction, so the same MARCH-to-lane action a that is correct at H_t is recorded with correct=false after the turn at H_t^tau. Success remains possible from H_t^tau by committing the opposite lane. At L3, a correct four-soldier commitment stops all four attackers, whereas the stale lane stops none and the four-ant breach removes all 3 home-queen HP. This strict loss is caused by the formation's changing task state, not by a deadline or later completion.

common_visible_process: The rival four-ant formation moves from its outpost toward the colony and visibly oscillates vertically through the NORTH/SOUTH intercept band. Its recent direction and reversal determine which tunnel commitment is correct at the delayed delivery time, and the same reversal makes a previously correct tunnel action lose its effect.

pre_run.reason: Every L3 generated world has one four-ant raid. The tunnel MARCH action is accepted only while that raid is inside its response band, and its correctness is sampled from the moving formation at the commit tick. A run that sends no further outcome-affecting actions after preparation cannot guarantee the required in-band interception. After the wave is resolved, MARCH to the rival queen is rejected until all raids are cleared and is required to reduce the rival queen's HP; there is no automatic victory. Thus no generated instance admits a successful action-free autonomous outcome phase under the normal visible controls.

source_evidence.claim: The assigned configuration is difficulty 3/full, with a 150-second allowance, an 800 ms observation window, and six frames per observation; L3 has five workers, two dig workers, a hidden opening, one seeded raid of count four, and the listed spawn/impact ticks.
The generator reads the exact control condition, derives the L3 parameters, chooses a seeded first lane, and validates the raid schedule.
Each generated raid has an expansion interval, response-open/deadline ticks, a spawn and impact tick, and a random motion phase offset.
The world uses a 100 ms tick, 18-tick gathering cycle, 14-tick production delay, 45-tick assault travel, and visible rules that require recent motion to choose a defense branch.
stepSimulation autonomously advances scouting, digging, gathering, production, raid readiness/impact, soldier assaults, queen damage, and the 720-tick terminal condition.

The browser accepts GATHER, SCOUT, DIG, RAISE, and MARCH; tunnel MARCH is available only for an uncommitted raid within response_open_tick through response_deadline_tick, and its commitment correctness is computed from interceptLane at the action tick.
raidWorldPosition moves the formation toward the colony and then gives it sinusoidal vertical motion; the vertical state is the visible temporal evidence for the intercept decision.
The live canvas renders the moving raid formation, intercept marker, tunnel lanes, and accumulated colony state.

Full mode uses map pointer selection/marquee, keyboard command arming, visible destination clicks, minimap/arrow panning, and an administrative certification button; the render loop continuously advances and redraws the state.
The grader computes the branch from the raid phase and motion offset, with the branch changing when the visible vertical direction reverses.

At impact, correct commitments filter living soldiers on the committed lane, stop up to the raid count, apply losses, and otherwise apply the breach to the home queen; the rival queen is damaged by completed assaults.
The replay grader rejects tunnel MARCH outside the visible response band and rejects rival-queen MARCH before all raids are cleared; accepted actions set the soldier orders and assault due tick.

The visible solver samples formation pixels at successive times and uses a consistent vertical delta as the observed advance vector, explicitly avoiding a turning point where the direction can expire before the pointer event.
The solver prepares the colony, raises enough soldiers before the first response band, then waits for visible contact and chooses a tunnel from successive visual measurements.
The shared clock distinguishes live and paused task time and advances the virtual task clock only while running.
A paused observation cycle runs a finite task-time window and then pauses at its endpoint, so the reported 800 ms horizon is task time rather than provider latency.
Verification loads the Anthill Front replay grader and grades the exported outcome, rather than treating the browser's visual path as the result itself.
